children: ACME will use the investment to advance green molecule facilities and expand its clean energy supply network across markets

Brookfield will invest up to USD 600 million in ACME Cleantech Ventures to support the development and construction of ACME Group’s green molecule projects across India and the Middle East. The investment will be made through Brookfield Global Transition Fund, according to a statement issued on 17 September.

ACME Cleantech Ventures is a UK-based privately held entity within the ACME Group dedicated to the group’s green molecule projects. The investment marks Brookfield’s entry into the green molecules sector in the region and combines its institutional capital and global scale with ACME’s operating capabilities.

ACME is advancing the development of green ammonia and green methanol facilities in India and Oman as part of its green molecules business. The company has also secured offtake partnerships with international and domestic counterparties, including Yara International, IHI Corporation, Mitsubishi Gas Chemicals and Solar Energy Corporation of India.

The company has an operational green ammonia facility in Bikaner, India, while it is developing another green ammonia project in Duqm, Oman. In India, Acme is also establishing new facilities in Odisha following its Green Ammonia Purchase Agreement with SECI, alongside a strategic joint venture with IHI Corporation and an offtake contract with Mitsubishi Gas Chemicals.

ACME's green molecules business is targeting sectors including fertilisers, shipping, refineries, chemicals and heavy industries. The company said its projects are focused on enabling green hydrogen and ammonia production for domestic and global markets, with the broader objective of supporting industries seeking to reduce emissions.

Manoj Upadhyay, Chairman of ACME Group, said, “Green molecules are creating a new supply chain for fuel and feedstock globally while strengthening the long-term energy security of nations.” He said the investment would support the development of green ammonia and other green molecule projects for customers across Asia, Europe and beyond.

Nawal Saini, Managing Partner and Head of Energy, South Asia and the Middle East, Brookfield, said demand for green molecules is growing as companies and governments seek scalable decarbonisation solutions while strengthening energy security. She said the investment brings together Brookfield’s global scale and institutional capital with ACME’s capabilities.

Brookfield is pursuing the investment through its Global Transition Fund strategy, which focuses on opportunities supporting the transition towards a net-zero carbon economy. The firm already has a significant renewable energy presence in India, with approximately 50 GW of wind and solar assets in operation and its pipeline across leading platforms.

ACME has secured offtake partnerships with Yara International, IHI Corporation, Mitsubishi Gas Chemicals and Indian fertiliser companies including IFFCO, Paradeep Phosphates, Coromandel International and Indorama India. The company said these partnerships provide a foundation for its green molecule projects and supply plans across domestic and international markets.
